land.text: Haripuñjaya (Lamphun), the Mon city-state of the Dvaravati world

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Dvaravati; Lopburi'. Cliopatria starts the row in 661 (the chronicle date, Camadevi 662-669); the page prefers c. 750.

land.text: the Ping valley round Lamphun and Lampang: 'Mangrai incorporated the kingdom into Lan Na'

successors.note: The infobox names Ngoenyang as the successor; Cliopatria's Lan Na Kingdom row starts in 1294. Phraya Yi Ba fled south to Lampang.

capitals.name: Haripuñjaya (Lamphun)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Haripuñjaya (Lamphun)'; the text gives no other capital or dates. Phraya Yi Ba, the last king, fled to Lampang when the city fell.

correction.text: The same outline is not drawn for 661-749: Mon city-states of the Dvaravati world, to be drawn from a Dvaravati dossier.

keyframe_review.note: Years 661-749 are before the state: the chronicles (Camadevivamsa, Jinakalamali) date the founding to 'between 629-57 AD' and give Camadevi 662-669, but the page says 'this date is now considered too early, and the actual beginning is placed at around 750 AD' and the infobox gives 'More probable founding of Haripunjaya: 750'. Cliopatria's 661 reflects the chronicle date.

correction.text: The same outline, drawn from 750 to 1065 (years only).

keyframe_review.note: Years only: 750-1065. The 143,044 km2 outline (from the Chiang Mai basin and Lamphun south to about 15.9 N) cannot be checked: the page gives no extent beyond Lampang (ruled by one of Camadevi's twins) and the Chiang Mai basin (Camadevi 'defeated Khun Luang Wilangka' at Raming Nakhon), both legendary, and no km2 figure; the Dong Mae Nang Mueang inscription (1167/8) at Nakhon Sawan was once attributed to a Haripunjaya king but Coedes preferred Lopburi. The Seshat page did not load.

141,821 km2: the same outline trimmed by about 1,200 km2; no page opened explains it. The page's 11th-century notes (Adityaraja's annexation of Lavo in 1052; invasions from Umongasela 'unsuccessful during the 10th-11th centuries') give no change of border. Unverified: page budget and page silence.

54,786 km2: the southern two-thirds (the Tak and upper Ping lands, 298 cells) are dropped, all of it inside Cliopatria's Khmer Empire shape of 1188, so the ledger records a confidence-1 loss to the Khmer Empire. The Haripunjaya page is silent on 1188 (rulers: Trangal 1195-1196, Notta 1196-1270, Niba/Yi Ba 1270-1292) and the Khmer Empire page on Haripunjaya; the Pagan page records Burmese chronicle claims of Chiang Mai under Sithu II (1174-1211) that most scholars reject. The northern core round Lamphun, Lampang and Chiang Mai stands (Lamphun inscriptions of 1213, 1218 and 1219 show the kingdom alive).

correction.text: The same outline, ended in 1292 (years only).

keyframe_review.note: Years only: 1285-1292. 'In 1292 the city was besieged and captured by Mangrai' (Haripunjaya page); the Mangrai page says 1291 ('Mangrai defeated the Mon kingdom and annexed Haripunjaya'); the Haripunjaya infobox gives 'Besieged and captured by Ngoenyang: 1281' and the page lists Yip as ruling to c. 1281 and Niba to 1292. Cliopatria ends the row in 1293.

ledger.note: c. 750: Haripunjaya arises at Lamphun. 'The actual beginning is placed at around 750 AD'; infobox 'More probable founding of Haripunjaya: 750' and 'Legendary founding of Haripunjaya by Suthep: 629'; the chronicles say four hermits founded it 'between 629-57 AD' and Camadevi, daughter of the Lavo king, was its first queen (662-669). Cliopatria starts in 661.

region.text: Lampang, the Chiang Mai basin and the rest of the northern outline, not dated by the page

ledger.counterpart: Lawa chiefdoms of Raming Nakhon (Khun Luang Wilangka)
ledger.note: c. 750: the rest of the realm. Page silent on dates: the legends have Jamadevi's twin ruling Lampang and Jamadevi defeating 'Khun Luang Wilangka' (the Lan Na version has him 'withdrawing to the hills') at Raming Nakhon (Chiang Mai). The Cliopatria outline is taken as the realm from the founding.

region.text: the Haripunjaya-Lavo frontier; the page names no place

ledger.note: 925: Haripunjaya and Lavo fight. 'Battles between Lavo and Haripunjaya are recorded from 925 to 927'; 'Rathasatkara of Haripunjaya moved south, and the Lavo king Uchitthaka Chakkawat defended'. The page gives no place.

region.text: the Haripunjaya-Lavo frontier; the page names no place

ledger.note: 927: the war ends as Tambralinga takes Lavo. The Dvaravati page: Uchitthaka 'lost Lavapura to Sujita of Tambralinga in 927 CE' and 'took Haripunjaya and ruled there until 930'.

927: a Lavo king takes the Haripunjaya throne. The rulers list has 'Uchitta jakraphad (King of Lavo) 927-930' between Traphaka (924-927) and Kampol (930-951); the Dvaravati page says the fugitive Uchitthaka 'took Haripunjaya and ruled there until 930'. A change of ruling line on the same land.

region.text: Lavo, ruled by the brother of Haripunjaya's king

ledger.note: 1052: Haripunjaya takes Lavo. Adityaraja 'annexed Lavo in 1052 and appointed his brother, Chadachota, the king of Lavo'; the Lavo page: 'Haripunjaya's Thamikaraj, with Suphannabhum's help, took Lavo' and Chandrachota reigned 1052-1069. Drawn as a dependency (the vassal is the Lavo dossier's state).

1082: Lavo's dependence ends. Page silent: Chandrachota's reign ended in 1069, a regent ruled 1069-1082 and Narai I, a new line, moved the capital to Ayodhya in 1082; the end of Haripunjaya's hold is bridged to that year.

region.text: the Tak and upper Ping lands in the south of the 1187 outline

ledger.note: 1188: the southern Haripunjaya lands pass to Angkor. Page silent: the Haripunjaya page does not mention 1188 or the Khmer Empire's frontier; the year and the land (298 cells, all inside Cliopatria's Khmer shape of 1188) are bridged from the Cliopatria change.

1292: Mangrai takes Hariphunchai. 'In 1292 the city was besieged and captured by Mangrai'; Mangrai 'incorporated the kingdom into Lan Na'. The Mangrai page gives 1291 and the Haripunjaya infobox 1281; Ai Fa's spying mission and Phraya Yi Ba's flight to Lampang are undated.

wars.name: Lavo-Haripunjaya war (925-927)
wars.outcome: 'Battles between Lavo and Haripunjaya are recorded from 925 to 927'; no border change on the pages. The Haripunjaya page is silent on the war.

wars.name: Haripunjaya's annexation of Lavo (1052)
wars.outcome: Adityaraja 'annexed Lavo in 1052 and appointed his brother, Chadachota, the king of Lavo'.
wars.note: The Haripunjaya page also says the Khmers 'took over Lavo from Tambralinga in 1002, and Haripunjaya came into conflict with them'.

wars.name: Conflict with the Khmers over Lavo (from 1002)
wars.outcome: 'The Khmers took over Lavo from Tambralinga in 1002, and Haripunjaya came into conflict with them'; the page gives no further date or border change.
wars.note: The Lavo page dates the Angkorian conquest differently (1001, c. 1005, 1006 or 1011-1014) and says it came from the east, not from Tambralinga.

wars.name: Invasions from Umongasela (10th-11th centuries)
wars.outcome: 'Invasions from Umongasela were unsuccessful during the 10th-11th centuries'; no border moved.
wars.note: The span is the two centuries the page names.

wars.name: Mangrai's conquest of Hariphunchai (1291-1292)
wars.outcome: 'In 1292 the city was besieged and captured by Mangrai' after his merchant Ai Fa had undermined King Yi Ba as chief minister; Yi Ba fled to Lampang; Mangrai made it part of Lan Na.
wars.note: The Mangrai page says 1291 and 'with the people in a state of discontent'; the infobox of the Haripunjaya page says 1281; the Mangrai page also has Yi Ba later driven 'further south, this time to Phitsanulok'.

certainty.note: A Mon mandala known from chronicles and inscriptions; no page opened gives a boundary, so every frontier (Lavo, the Khmer lands, the Shan hills, Pagan's cis-Salween claims) is approximate.

sources.title: Haripuñjaya
sources.note: Identity; founding c. 750 (legendary 629-57); Camadevi and Lavo; Lampang and Chiang Mai legends; 1052 annexation of Lavo; Mangrai's capture 1292 (infobox 1281); rulers list (with gaps). No km2 figure.

sources.title: Lavo Kingdom
sources.note: Battles with Lavo 925-927; Tambralinga 927-946; 1052 Haripunjaya and Suphannabhum take Lavo; Chandrachota 1052-1069.

sources.title: Mangrai
sources.note: Mangrai defeated the Mon kingdom and annexed Haripunjaya in 1291; Ai Fa's spying mission; Yi Ba's flight to Lampang and Phitsanulok; Chiang Mai 1296.

sources.title: Dvaravati
sources.note: Dvaravati as a cultural sphere; Uchitthaka lost Lavapura in 927 and 'took Haripunjaya and ruled there until 930'.

sources.title: Pagan Kingdom
sources.note: Opened for the Burmese frontier: silent on Haripunjaya; Burmese chronicles' claim of Chiang Mai under Sithu II (1174-1211), which most scholars reject; Pagan's reach stops at the Salween.

sources.title: Sukhothai Kingdom
sources.note: Opened for the Sukhothai frontier of 1241-1293: silent on Haripunjaya in Ram Khamhaeng's time; Lan Na not listed as his territory.

notes: Cliopatria's row (661-1293, five shapes, a constant 143,044 km2 outline to 1065 and a 54,786 km2 one from 1188) is kept as one state; the 'spans 632 years' flag is not a succession of states but a Mon kingdom with a chronicle founding and a Lan Na conquest. Moved from Cliopatria: start c. 750 (not 661), the page's 'more probable' founding, with the chronicle date 662 kept in the keyframe note; end 1292 (not 1293), three dates on two pages (1281 infobox, 1291 Mangrai, 1292 text). Not settled: the extent of the realm (no page gives one; the outline of 143,000 km2 is unverified and was not compared to an infobox area because the page gives none); the 1188 loss of the south to the Khmer Empire (confidence 1, bridged from Cliopatria); the end of Haripunjaya's hold on Lavo (conf 1, 1082); the fate of Yi Ba's rump at Lampang; Pagan's claimed overlordship of Chiang Mai in 1174-1211 (chronicle claim, not drawn). The Seshat page th_haribhunjaya_k did not load. No rulers list: the chronicle list has gaps of 30-80 years. Counterparts: dvaravati (no row, no dossier; additions batch se-01-x); lavo-kingdom (this batch); khmer-empire (should carry the gain of 1188); lan-na-kingdom (starts 1294 in Cliopatria; should carry the gain of 1292 and the 1291-1294 gap); suphannaphum (Suphannabhum, no row).
